description: We are a team of motivated students participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Ben Guerir. Our team, brings together students with backgrounds in Python, web development, artificial intelligence, and design. We are interested in using technology and creativity to solve real-world challenges related to space exploration.
summary:
We created AstroCare, a transparent health self-assessment interface specifically intended for extended space missions. This software analyzes vital signs, activities, and emotional states recorded by astronauts, compares them to set parameters, and promptly categorizes each input as either Normal, Watch, or Escalate, accompanied by a detailed explanation.

AstroCare solves the problem of communication delays in deep space by providing independent, on-board support instead of depending on obscure, "black box" algorithms. It addresses sensor discrepancies clearly, marking all telemetry as measured, calculated, simulated, or absent. Additionally, its configuration-based architecture utilizes a JSON indicator library, which enables the system to integrate new hardware effortlessly without the need to alter the core programming.

This initiative holds significant importance as ongoing monitoring of both physical and mental health is critical, whereas ground delays make real-time support impossible. AstroCare creates a repeatable model for crew safety that emphasizes data transparency and minimizes cognitive burden, ensuring that astronauts receive prompt assistance while keeping flight surgeons informed to make the ultimate decisions.
details: AstroCare serves as an intelligent and transparent health-monitoring dashboard tailored for astronauts on extended space missions, like journeys to the Moon or Mars, where significant communication delays prevent real-time assistance from Earth. When an astronaut enters daily information—covering identified NASA risks such as cardiovascular deconditioning, muscle and bone deterioration, mental health, and radiation exposure—the application promptly assesses the information against medical benchmarks. It delivers a straightforward, color-coded status of "Normal," "Watch," or "Escalate," accompanied by a simple written explanation, and arranges these indicators on a body map, enabling crew members to review their data similarly to a medical professional. AstroCare maintains transparency in its operations, proactively informs users if any telemetry data is absent, and clearly categorizes all information as measured, calculated, simulated, or not yet assimilated. Developed with Python, Streamlit, and Pandas for tracking historical data, along with Plotly for interactive graphical representations, the platform features a high-contrast design aimed at minimizing cognitive strain during high-pressure scenarios. It can conveniently incorporate new medical sensors through JSON files without the need to alter the foundational code, functioning as a nimble prototype now and as a reusable framework for the future, while guaranteeing that flight surgeons on Earth retain the ultimate authority in clinical decision-making.
